Detergent. That which cleanses or washes away.

The transverse lines cutting vertical ones at right angles, to show by a diagram the relations of two series of facts, as, e. g., the number of pulse-beats, or the temperature record in given periods of time.
A disorder in the syntactical arrangement of uttered speech, due to some central lesion.
Methyl cyanid. It is a colorless liquid.
Asphyxia of the extremities, the so-called phenomena of Raynaud.
A fatty substance derived from sheep's wool.
Inulol. An aromatic liquid obtained from elecampane ; used like creosote in pulmonary tuberculosis.
The supposed art of the transmutation of metals (into gold) and of finding a remedy for all diseases.
An instrument for estimating the alkali in a substance.

A chemic compound produced by the substitution of an acid radicle for one or more of the hydrogen atoms of ammonia. The amids are primary, secondary, or tertiary, according as one, two, or three hydrogen atoms have been so replaced.

A colorless, pungent gas, NH3, very soluble in water. The preparations of ammonium are used as antacids and as gastric and cardiac stimulants, in headache, hysteria, etc. It is a stimulant to the heart, and, in its elimination through the lungs, stimulates and liquefies the bronchial secretion.
An instrument for estimating the current of an electric circuit in amperes.
Uncertain ; doubtful. Applied to a period in the febrile process occurring between the fastigium and the defervescence, and marked by exacerbations and remissions.
An accumulation of serum in the subcutaneous areolar tissues of the body.
An hermaphrodite ; a female in whom the genital organs are similar to those of the male.

Deficiency of blood as a whole, or deficiency of the number of the red corpuscles, or of the hemoglobin. It may be general or local. Local anemia, or ischemia, is the result of mechanical interference with the circulation of the affected part. General anemia is either idiopathic or symptomatic.
Pertaining to or characterized by anencephalia.
To put under the influence of an anesthetic.
Any disease attended by a sense of choking or suffocation, particularly an affection of the fauces or pharynx presenting such symptoms.
An animal organism so small as to require the microscope for its examination.
A crystalline alkaloid, a derivative of anise.
Annatto, arnotto. A coloring matter obtained from the pellicles of the seeds of Bixa orellana. It is used to color plasters, and as an artificial color for butter.
1. A defect in vision in which straight lines do not seem straight, and parallelism or symmetry is not properly perceived. 2. Squinting ; obliquity of vision.
1. A carbuncle. 2. An acute infectious disease due to the bacillus anthracis. It is most common in cattle and sheep, but may occur in man.
1. Preventing or checking salivation. 2. A remedy that is effective against salivation.

A counter poison or antidote elaborated by the body to counteract the toxins of bacteria. According to some authorities, antitoxins are, like the toxins, bacterial products. Antitoxins are used in the treatment of certain infectious diseases and also to confer immunity against these diseases.
1. Preventing or checking fermentation. 2. An agent preventing the process of fermentation ; an antiferment.

A structure having a curved outline resembling that of an arc or a bow. A., Aortic, five pairs of vascular arches existing in the fetus. A., Branchial, the cartilaginous arches that support the gills of fishes. In the human fetus they are also present. A., Crural, Poupart's ligament.
An ointment containing grs. viiss of belladonna to " ]% of blue ointment.

1. Having a spicy odor. 2. A substance characterized by a fragrant, spicy taste and odor, as cinnamon, ginger, the essential oils, etc. 3. A qualification applied to any carbon compound originating from benzin, C6H6. Their stability is relatively great as compared with that of the fatty bodies.
The process of making or becoming arterial ; the change from venous blood into arterial.
1. A description of the arteries. 2. The graphic representation of the pulse waves.
A bitter glucosid obtainable from various species of Asclepias. It is poisonous, and has emetic, purgative, and sudorific properties, Unof.

A species of omphalositic monster characterized by an absence of the trunk. The head is never well-formed, and the vessels run from it to the placenta in the membranes. Beneath the head is a sac in which rudiments of body-organs may be found. This is the rarest form of omphalosites.
An apparatus for withdrawing liquids from cavities by means of suction.
The common mesal cavity of the cerebrum, it being also the anterior portion of the third ventricle.
The spontaneous or self-cure of a disease.
Toxemia from poisons derived from the organism itself.
Applied to parts that are single, not in pairs.

Bacillus cuneatus. Syn., Bacterimn cuneatum, Rivolta. Found in the blood and viscera of horses, cattle, and dogs dead of septic processes, pg. Bacillus cuniculicidus, Koch. See Bacillus septicemia hcemorrhagica , Sternberg. Bacillus cuniculicida havaniensis, Sternberg.
Systematic bathing for therapeutic purposes, or the treatment of disease by baths.
The passage of urine having a high specific gravity ; also the condition of the body associated therewith.

The lowest part of a body or the foundation upon which anything rests. In chemistry, an element or radicle that combines with an acid to form a salt. The electropositive molecule or radicle of a compound. In pharmacy, the most important part of a prescription.
A point located at the middle of the anterior margin of the foramen magnum.
Leaf-cup. A composite-flowered plant, Polymnia uvedalia of N. America. A popular remedy for enlargement of the spleen, or the "ague-cake" of malarious regions.

The radicle of benzoic acid, of oil of bitter almonds, and of an extensive series of compounds derived from this oil, or connected with it by certain relations. B.- ecgonin, C16H18N04H, a substance intermediate in composition between cocain and ecgonin. B.-glycocoll. See Acid, Hippuric.
Having two heads, a term applied to several muscles, as B. brachii, B. extensor, B. flexor cruris.
The science embracing the structure, function, and organization of living forms.

Any tree of the genus Betula. Birch-tar, or the tarry oil of B. alba, is useful in certain skin-diseases. The bark of B. lenta, the American black birch, yields a fragrant volatile oil, identical with that of Gaultheria procumbens, for which it is extensively substituted.
A brown, basic anilin dye, extensively used as a stain and counterstain in histology.
In chemistry, a valence or saturating power double that of the hydrogen atom.
Any one of the nucleated cells or segments into which the fecundated vitellus divides.

Linseed oil that has been heated to a high temperature (1300 C. and upward), while a current of air is passed through or over the oil, and the temperature increased until the oil begins to effervesce from evolution of products of decomposition.

Bog-bean. The rhizome of Menyanthestrifoliata, tonic, antiscorbutic, and emmenagogue. It has been recommended as a vermifuge, and has been used in functional amenorrhea. Dose of fid. ext., TT^v-xxx (0.32-2 o). Unof.
A name sometimes given to the glands of Bartholin.

A ptomain, occurring very frequently in decomposing animal tissues. It is obtained from human hearts, lungs, livers, etc., after three days' decomposition at ordinary temperature, - also from horseflesh, from putrid mussel, from herring, and haddock.
The power of holding or containing ; mental or physical ability. C, Vital, the total amount of air that can be expelled by the most forcible expiration after the deepest inspiration.
Relating to the lens and to its capsule.
The recurrent monthly discharge of blood during
A popular name for various plants of the genera Centaurea, Eiythrcea, Sabbatia, Chlora, etc. It is used as a simple, bitter tonic. Dose ss-j in decoction several times a day. Unof.
An order of mammals living in the sea, as the whale, dolphin, etc,

A term formerly used indiscriminately for any primary venereal ulcer, but now generally applied to the initial lesion of syphilis (see Syphilis). C, Hard, Hunterian, Indurated, Infecting, Non-suppurating, or True, the ulcer of venereal origin, that is followed by constitutional syphilis.

The destruction of bacteria by phagocytes ; the victory of the phagocytes over bacteria, or of bacteria over phagocytes. In biology, the attraction of leukocytes by certain chemic substances held in solution in the blood. Cf. Chemotaxis.
Melanoderma; melasma; discolorations. A deposit of pigment in the skin, occurring in patches of various sizes and shapes, and of a yellow, brown, or black color.
The artificial establishment of a communication between the gall-bladder and the intestine.
The outermost of the fetal membranes, formed from the vitelline membrane, the false amnion, and the allantois. The chorion lies between the amnion and thedeciduae (reflexa and vera).
A disorder of vision in which color-impressions arise subjectively. It may be due to disturbance of the optic centers, or to drugs, especially santonin.

A rare condition of the sweat in which it is variously colored, being bluish, blackish, reddish, greenish, or yellowish. Black szveat {Seborrhcea nigricans) occurs usually in hysteric women, the face being most often affected.
Food that has undergone gastric digestion and has not yet been acted upon by the biliary, pancreatic, and intestinal secretions.
Relating to the ciliary zone and the spine.
The plant Artemisia santonica. See Santonica.
An alkaloid derived from cinchona. It is a crystalline substance resembling quinin in general properties.
C. Agent, a substance used in microscopy to render tissues transparent and suitable for mounting.
An instrument for measuring the degree of inclination of the pelvic axis.
The dried fruit of Anamirta cocculus. It is an active narcotic poison. It is employed as a destroyer of vermin. See Picrotoxin.

A cavity of the internal ear resembling a snail-shell. It describes two and a half turns about a central pillar called the modiolus or columnella, forming the spiral canal, about 1^4. inches in length. See also Ear.
The larva of Tenia ccenurus (Ktichenmeister), producing the disease of sheep called staggers.

Meadow-saffron. The corm and seed of C. autumnale, the properties of which are due to an alkaloid, colchicin. It is an emetic, diuretic, diaphoretic, and drastic cathartic. It is valuable in acute gout, and in some forms of rheumatism.
A ptomain, isomeric but not identical with aldehyd-collidin. The ptomain was obtained from pancreas and gelatin allowed to putrefy together in water.
The liquefaction or breaking down of a tissue or organ.
Unconsciousness from which the patient cannot be aroused by external stimulus. C, Alcoholic, that due to poisoning by alcohol. C Apoplectic, that due to apoplexy. C., Uremic, that due to uremia.
One part of sodium or potassium permanganate dissolved in 500 parts of water ; it is a useful disinfectant.
The abnormal union of two contiguous surfaces or bodies, as of two fingers, or of the opposed surfaces of the pleural or pericardial sac.
A red coloring-matter which becomes blue in the presence of free HC1. It is used in chemic investigation of the gastric juice.
A series of conic masses of tubules that together form the globus major of the epididymis.
An alkaline substance, a normal constituent of urine. It crystallizes in rhombic prisms, and is a strong base. It is much more soluble than creatin.

The process by which the molecules of a substance arrange themselves in geometric forms when passing from a gaseous or a liquid to a solid state. C, Water of, the water of salts that cannot be extracted without destruction of their crystalline nature.
Having the upper surface depressed ; applied to the coagulum of blood after phlebotomy.
A soft, red clot seen post-mortem in the heart and blood-vessels.
The embryo of a tapeworm when it has reached the encysted stage. An hydatid.
1. A muscle, instrument, or apparatus that depresses. 2. A nerve, stimulation of which lowers the functional activity of a part, as the depressor nerve of the heart.
The elastic membrane lining the posterior surface of the cornea.
Transposition of the heart to the right side of the thorax.
A disease characterized by the habitual discharge of an excessive quantity of urine ; used without qualification, the word indicates diabetes mellitus, D., Bil-
An apparatus for effecting dialysis ; also the porous septum or diaphragm of such an apparatus.
A compound consisting of an element or radicle and two atoms of bromin.
A compound resulting from the replacement of the hydrogen of two molecules of nitric acid by a base.
Oleum cornu cervi. An oil obtained in distilling bone and deer's horn. It contains pyridin and lutidin. It is antispasmodic and stimulant. Unof.

Separation, especially the separation of a complex compound into simpler molecules by the action of heat. D.- symptom, anesthesia to pain and to heat and cold, with preservation of tactile sensibility and of the muscular sense ; it is observed in syringomyelia.
The determination of the proper amount of
A substance used as a medicine. D., Antagonistic, one that neutralizes the action of another.
The operation of forming an opening into the duodenum through the abdominal walls.
Relating to, or of the nature of, eclampsia.
The outer of the two primitive layers of the embryo.
The outer, hyaline, more compact layer of protoplasm of a cell or unicellular organism.
The dried sediment from the juice of the squirting cucumber, Ecballium elaterium. It is a powerful hydragogue cathartic. Dose y% gr. (0.008).

A projecting, prominent part of an organ, especially of a bone. E., Canine. See Canine. E., Collateral, a projection in the lateral ventricle of the brain between the middle and posterior horns. E., Frontal, the two eminences of the frontal bone above the superciliary ridges.
Tonic muscular spasm in which the body is bent forward.
A double monstrosity, with practically complete and functionating organs, but united with a more or less superficial bond.
Hernia in which both bowel and omentum are involved.
An exceptional sequence or unusual complication arising in the course of a disease.
A process of bone attached for a time to another bone by cartilage, but in most
An animal parasite living upon the exterior of the body.
Slow oxidation or gradual decay, without combustion.
An abnormality of vision in which all objects appear red ; red vision.
Opening of the esophagus by an incision.
Outside of the proper structures of a joint.
The unit of electric capacity; a capacity sufficient to hold one coulomb of current having a potential of one volt.
The application of the induced current to a part.
The ground or powdered starchy part of seeds, especially that of corn, barley, rye, and wheat.
A solution used for rinsing the pharynx and nasopharynx.

An air-like fluid. The word is especially applied to those fluids that under normal conditions are aeriform ; while those that can be readily condensed to liquids are termed vapors. G., Laughing, nitrous oxid. G., Marsh, methane. G., Olefiant, ethylene.
A bandage for fracture of the lower jaw.
The chronic stage of urethritis characterized by a slight mucopurulent discharge.
A crystalline acid found in decomposed pus.
Of the nature of gout; affected with gout.

The Mikania guaco and other species of Mikania and Aristolochia, used in South America* for snakebites ; it has been employed in rheumatism, gout, and in various skin-diseases. Dose of a watery extract gr. iij (0.19).

A concrete vegetable juice exuded from many plants. When treated with nitric acid it yields mucic acid. Gums are either entirely soluble in water, or swell up in it into a viscid mass. Various names are given to gums, usually indicating the place whence exported.
Dulness of the special senses and intellect ; a condition present in grave fevers.
Crystals of ammonium urate found as a urinary deposit in the form of globular crystals, with spiny projections.
An instrument used in the spectroscopic examination of the blood, by means of which the thickness of the layer of blood can be regulated.
Cannabis sativa, the bast-fiber of which is used for textile purposes. H., Indian. See Cannabis indica.
A cyst-like body with clear contents, especially that formed by the larva of the Taenia echinococcus.
An acid formed by a combination of hydrogen and an acid element or radicle other than oxygen.
1. Expelling water. 2. A purgative that causes copious liquid discharges.

1. Diamid; a colorless, stable, gas, soluble in water, having a peculiar odor, and a strong alkaline reaction. 2. One of a class of bodies derived from hydrazin by replacing one or more of its hydrogen atoms by a radicle.
Pertaining to electricity developed in connection with water.
A collection of serum within the pericardial cavity.
An acute infectious disease communicated to man by the bites of animals suffering from rabies. The period of incubation is variable, the average being from three to six months.
The presence of hydrogen sulphid in the urine.
Affected with marked or delayed dicrotism ; a condition in which the aortic notch is below the base-line.
Excessive blood in a part. H., Active, that caused by an excessive supply of blood going to a part. H., Passive, that caused by an impediment to the removal of the blood.
Excessive movement, as that, associated with muscular spasm.
Excessive formation of tissue ; an increase in the size of a tissue or organ owing to an increase in the number of cells ; also termed numerical hypertrophy.
Excessively high body-temperature. By some the term is used only when the temperature is above 1060 F.
Placed or introduced beneath the skin, as H. injection.
Having the lower mandible longer than the upper.
The fleshy eminence on the palm of the hand over the metacarpal bone of the little finger. Also, the prominences on the palm at the base of the fingers.

A diseased state of the mind manifesting itself in countless disturbances of the psychic, sensory, motor, and vasomotor functions. The etiology is not definitely known ; heredity and mental shock play an important part.
A form of hysteria accompanied by convulsions resembling those of epilepsy.

Isinglass. The air-bladder of the sturgeon, Acipenser huso, occurring in horny, translucent, white sheets, that form a jelly with hot water. It is a form of gelatin, and is used as a food, for clarifying liquids, and as a test for tannic acid. I., Emplastrum, court-plaster.

Pertaining to the ilium or to the flanks. 1. Artery. See Arteries, Tabic of. 1. Crest, the upper free margin of the ilium to which the abdominal muscles are attached. 1. Fascia, the fascia lining the posterior part of the abdominal cavity and covering the psoas andilincus
A prefix denoting relation to the ilium.

I . The act of illuminating or lighting up. 2. The quantity of light thrown on an object. I., critical, in microscopy, an illumination in which the lamp-flame is focused on the object. I., Direct, illumination of an object by light thrown upon it from in front.
A slight illness not confining the patient to bed.

A substance produced in pancreatic digestion, in intestinal putrefaction, and in certain bacterial cultures. It occurs in the feces, giving to them in part their odor, and is eliminated in the urine in the form of indican, being especially increased in intestinal obstruction.

Hardening; the state of being or becoming hard ; a hardened mass or lump. I., Brown, a form of interstitial pneumonia in which there is, in addition to the new growth of fibrous tissue, a deposit of altered bloodpigment. I., Gray, a similar condition without the deposit of pigment.
An instrument for inhaling a gas or vapor.
Coming on stealthily or imperceptibly. 1. Disease, one, the onset of which is gradual or inappreciable.
To make thick by evaporation or by absorption of fluid.
The act of making intense, or of increasing the strength of anything.
Marriage between persons related by consanguinity, or between persons of different races.
Between the maxillary bones. 1. Bone, the small bone that receives the incisors, situated between the superior maxillary bones of the fetus.
Situated between the cerebral or cerebellar peduncles. 1. Space, the pons Tarini, or posterior perforated space that forms the posterior portion of the floor of the third ventricle.

The quality of being isomeric. 1. is of two kinds - (a) substances may have the same percentage-composition and the same molecular weights ; these are termed metameric ; (b) they may have the same percentage-composition, but different molecular weights ; these are termed polymeric.
A genus of the order Acaridea, including most of the parasitic ticks.

1. A unit of electric energy, equivalent to the work expended when a current of one ampere flows for one second against a resistance of one ohm. 2. A small calorie - the amount of heat required to raise the gram of water 1 degrees C.
Situation adjacent to another; the act of placing near; apposition.
Methylquinolin hydrid. An antipyretic resembling kairin, but less efficient.
Pertaining to karyokinesis, as K. figures, the forms assumed by the mitome in karyokinesis.
A knife with a peculiar trowel - like blade, used for making the incision into the cornea in the operation of iridectomy.
An operation for repairing an injured or diseased lip ; chiloplasty.
A proteid contained in milk; it resembles serum-albumin, and coagulates at a temperature of from 700 to 8o degrees C.
Suckling ; the period during which the child is nourished from the breast.
The downlike hair that appears upon the fetus at about the fifth month of gestation ; also the downy growth often seen upon the face of women and girls.
1. Suprapubic cystotomy. 2. An operation in advanced extrauterine pregnancy for the removal of the fetus, the sac being allowed to remain.
The operation of cutting into the uterus through an abdominal incision, as for the purpose of removing a fetus. .
The science of the anatomy, physiology, and diseases of the larynx.
The sound of the voice observed in auscultation of the larynx.
1. A condition marked by a tendency to dropsy, accompanied by a pale, flabby skin, and general edema of the whole body; solid edema. 2. Phlegmasia alba dolens.
A carbohydrate prepared by heating levulose.
Inflammation of the bursa over the tuberosity of the ischium, from much sitting.
A method of treatment of disease by gymnastic and other rhythmic movements of the body, employed by Ling, a Swedish physician ; kinesitherapy.
The largest gland in the body, situated on the right side of the abdominal cavity, just below the. diaphragm, and forming an appendage of the digestive tract.
Pertaining to the moon or to silver {luna of the alchemists).

The organ of respiration, in which the impure venous blood is oxidized by the air drawn through the trachea and bronchi into the air- vesicles. There are two lungs, a right and a left, the former usually consisting of three, the latter of two lobes.
The process of softening a solid substance, or of converting into a soft mass by soaking in a liquid, as, e.g., M. of the fetus.
1. Pertaining to the male sex, that which impregnates the female. 2. A member of the male sex. 3. Of a double-bladed instrument, the blade which is received into a hollow of the other (female) blade.

A febrile disease prevalent on the coasts bordering on the Mediterranean. It is characterized by malaise, an irregular fever, rigors, headache, pains in the limbs, and diarrhea ; and frequent relapses. The etiology is not definitely known ; some of the cases are probably forms of typhoid fever.
The breast; the milk-secreting gland of the mother.
Pertaining conjointly to medicine and surgery.
A liquid hydrocarbon produced when menthol is distilled with phosphorus pentoxid.
1. Pertaining to or caused by mercury. 2. Any preparation of mercury or its salts.
A bacterium multiplying by two rectangular divisions, thus forming a tablet-like group of four cells in one plane.
Pertaining to or situated in the middle line or plane.
An instrument for giving uterine douches.
A large uninuclear spheroidal cell the protoplasm of which contains hemoglobin, and which is supposed to be the source of the red corpuscles of the blood.
An instrument designed for measuring minute objects seen through the microscope. M., Eye-piece, M., Ocular, a micrometer to be used with the eye-piece of a microscope.
The millionth part of a meter or a thousandth part of a millimeter. It is the equivalent of T5?oir degrees f an English inch, and its symbol is \i.
Mixture of different races by intermarriage.
The threads of the protoplasmic reticulum of a cell (cytomitome) or of the nucleus (karyomitome) .
Paralysis of a single part of the body, as of one limb.
Pertaining to, affected with, or of the nature of, myxedema.
The condition resulting from the use of a narcotic.
The space between the posterior nares and a horizontal plane through the lower margin of the soft palate.

The pnnctum proximum, the point nearest the eye at which an object can be seen distinctly. N., Absolute, that nearpoint for either eye alone at which no effort at accommodation is made. N., Relative, that near-point for both eyes at which accommodation is brought into play.
Incision of the kidney. N., Abdominal, one through an abdominal incision. N., Lumbar, one through an incision in the loin.
Pertaining to the embryonic neural canal and the intestinal tube.

A tumor springing from a nerve. It is a true N. when made up of nervous tissue proper, and a false N. when consisting of other than nervous tissue. False neuromas may be fibromas, myxomas, gliomas, etc. N., Amputation-, the neuroma of a stump, forming at the end of a divided nerve.
A name applied to plants of the genus Solanum. N., Deadly, the Atropa belladonna.
Bacteria that convert ammonia into nitric acid.
A long, flexible tube used in making rectal injections.
Olefiant gas ; also any one of a series of unsaturated hydrocarbons having the formula
An instrument for determining the power of smell.
A deficiency of red corpuscles in the blood.
Insanity in which only a few of the mental faculties are deranged.
An instrument for examination of the eye through a layer of water, whereby the curvature, and hence the refraction of the cornea, is neutralized and the cornea acts as a plane medium.
The study of diseases of the ear and their treatment.
The science of the ear, its anatomy, functions, and diseases.
A varicocele of the veins of the pampiniform plexus.
Puncture; especially puncture of the wall of a cavity of the body, such as the thoracic wall, cornea, tympanic membrane.
Disturbance of the power of reading, consisting in the transposition or substitution of words or syllables.
Difficulty in thinking logically. P., Thematic, a condition in which the thought is unduly concentrated on one subject. .
Pertaining to the parietal and temporal bones.
Syphilitic pseudoparalysis. See Diseases, Table of.
1. A synthetic liquid base. 2. A ptomain isomeric with it, occurring in decomposing fish and horseflesh.
Resembling or having the nature of pemphigus.

An instrument for measuring the extent of the field of vision. It consists ordinarily of a flat, narrow metal plate, bent in a semicircle, graduated in degrees, and fixed to an upright at its center by a pivot, on which it is movable.

1. The secretion of sweat. 2. The sweat. P., Insensible, that which takes place constantly, the fluid being evaporated as fast as secreted. P., Sensible, that accumulating in visible drops or beads ; the sweat.
The art of preparing, compounding, and dispensing medicines. 2. A drug-store.
Disease of the pharynx due to the action of fungi.
An instrument for use in examining the pharynx.

A subjective sensation of light or color, as, e.g., scotoma scintillans. Aphose, a subjective sensation of shadow or darkness, as, e. g., muscse volitantes. Centraphoses, aphoses originating in the optic centers. Centrophoses, phoses originating in the optic centers.
An instrument for measuring the intensity of light.
A craving for unnatural and strange articles of food; a symptom present in certain forms of insanity, hysteria, and chlorosis, and during pregnancy.
A columnar structure acting as a support.
A medicine given for the purpose of pleasing or humoring the patient, rather than for its therapeutic effect.
A prefix denoting pertaining to the lungs.
Potassium hydroxid, caustic potash. 2. Potassium carbonate.
Preceding the dicrotic wave or elevation of the sphygmographic tracing.

1. Pertaining to a profession, especially to the medical profession ; in keeping with medical ethics. 2. Produced by the practice of a profession, as P. neurosis (writer's cramp, telegrapher's cramp, etc.).
Deep-seated ; applied to certain muscles, and in the feminine, profunda, to certain arteries. See Arteries, Table of.
A crystalline glucosid found in nervous tissue, and yield ing when boiled with baryta the decomposition-products of lecithin.
Pertaining to, characterized by, or effecting, proteolysis.
Any one of a group of bodies formed in gastric digestion, intermediate between the food-proteids and the peptones, called antipeptone, hemipeptone, etc.
A chronic inflammatory disease of the skin, characterized by the development of reddish patches covered with whitish scales. The disease affects especially the extensor surfaces of the body.
In chemistry, applied to an acid having four replaceable hydrogen-atoms.
Affected with, resembling, or produced by rachitis ; rickety.
A seam or ridge, especially one indicating the line of junction of two symmetric halves.
Pertaining to or of the rjature of a recrement.
Pertaining to the rectum and the uterus.
Inoculation a second time with the same kind of virus.
An acute infectious disease due to thespirocha^taObermaieri. After a period of incubation of from five to seven days, the disease sets in with chill, fever, and pains in the back and limbs.
A red pigment found in the retinal cones.
The name given to the bowel-discharges in cholera.
Jacob's Ulcer ; noli me tangere ; a superficial ulceration of the skin, occurring usually in the eyelid or the side of the nose, and frequently persisting for years ; it is a form of epithelioma.
The act of converting into soap ; the process of treating a neutral fat with an alkali, which combines with the fatty acid, forming a soap.
A poisonous glucosid obtained from saponin.
An instrument having a thin blade with sharp teeth on one edge, and used for dividing bones and other hard substances. S., Butcher's, one in which the blade can be fixed at any angle.
The deep layer of the superficial abdominal fascia.
Pertaining to or of the nature of a schema.
Pertaining conjointly to the sclerotic coat and the cornea of the eye.
The placenta, part of the umbilicus, and the membranes discharged from the uterus after the birth of the child.
Half; abbreviated in prescription to ss., which is placed after the sign indicating the measure.
Transverse or perpendicular fibers transfixing and joining the lamella; of bone.
A form of monster in which the lower extremities are intimately fused, the feet being absent.
The process of converting into a skeleton ; gradual wasting of the soft parts, leaving only the skeleton.
The periodic state of rest in which voluntary consciousness and activity cease.
An occupation-neurosis occurring in smiths and characterized by painful cramps in the arm or hand.
A convulsive inspiration due to contraction of the diaphragm and spasmodic closure of the glottis.
1. The faculty of expressing thought by spoken words ; the act of speaking. 2. The words spoken.
A formative seminal cell or mass of spermatoblasts.
A prefix denoting pertaining to the sphenoid bone.
Pertaining to or produced by waste-material, as, e.g., S. enlargement of the spleen, a swelling of the spleen produced by the accumulation of the detritus of red corpuscles.
An apparatus for destroying the microorganisms attached to an object, especially by means of heat.
A prefix denoting connection with the sternum.
Pertaining to the sternum and the trachea.
An instrument for measuring the phenomena elicited by auscultation.

An instrument for ascertaining the condition of the organs of circulation and respiration by the sounds made by these organs. It consists of a hollow tube, one end being placed over the locality to be examined, the other at the ear of the examiner.
